items.title: Derrick Gardner interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 9, 2013
items.q: There is one tune that Shirley Horn made famous, called “Here’s to Life,” man. And Joe Williams did it.

ctx.x: Joe Williams. Oh man. It was such a — I felt like I was in school the entire time when we got the chance to perform with Joe Williams along with the Basie band. We did several tours with him. And wow. His sense of phrasing and timing, and the way that he just treats a tune was impeccable. Every note and every lyric that he sang was perfectly placed. Almost like he was reading from a page. And he was able to take an audience and just put the audience right in his hand, and the whole audience is just like that —…

You know, we’ve got to get you to your thing. But this has really been fascinating. And one of the best kinds of compliments a person gets is somebody that wasn’t drawn out. One of my saxophone students, Brett, who played with you on the jam session last night, and he said “I really liked that guy. He didn’t play a gazillion notes like some of the other people, and every note seemed to mean something.” He said that about you.
